questions.prompt: What is the role of a browser driver such as chromedriver or geckodriver?
options: It receives W3C WebDriver commands over HTTP and controls the browser
questions.explanation: Client libraries send commands to the driver, which translates them into browser automation. The browser renders pages; the test runner runs tests.

questions.prompt: Selenium Manager (bundled since Selenium 4.6) can locate or download a matching driver automatically when none is configured.
questions.explanation: Selenium Manager resolves drivers (and can download browsers) so most local setups no longer need System.setProperty or a separate driver manager.

questions.prompt: Which Selenium component lets you run tests on many machines and browsers from one endpoint?
questions.explanation: Grid routes sessions to nodes. IDE records tests in the browser; Manager resolves drivers; BiDi is a bidirectional protocol for events such as console logs.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP request does the client send for `driver.findElement(By.id("q"))` under the W3C protocol?
questions.explanation: W3C WebDriver has five location strategies (css selector, link text, partial link text, tag name, xpath); the Java client translates By.id into a CSS selector and POSTs to /session/{id}/element.

questions.prompt: Tests fail with 'session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version N'. What is the cause and the modern fix?
options: The driver and browser versions do not match; let Selenium Manager pick the right driver (remove the hard-coded driver path) or update the driver
Use Thread.sleep before creating the driver
questions.explanation: Each chromedriver major version supports a matching Chrome major version. A stale pinned driver path breaks after Chrome auto-updates; Selenium Manager resolves a compatible driver.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the W3C WebDriver protocol are true? Select all that apply.
options: Commands are HTTP requests with JSON bodies
Each command targets a session created with POST /session
It is a W3C Recommendation implemented by major browser vendors' drivers
It streams browser events to the client over a WebSocket
questions.explanation: Classic WebDriver is request/response over HTTP. Event streaming over WebSocket is WebDriver BiDi, a separate (newer) specification.

questions.prompt: What does `driver.quit()` do that `driver.close()` does not?
options: Ends the whole session: closes every window and shuts down the driver process
Clears cookies but keeps the browser open
questions.explanation: close() closes the current window; when it is the last one, the session may end, but quit() reliably ends the session and frees resources. Always call quit() in teardown.

questions.prompt: Tests on Selenium Grid queue for minutes before starting, while nodes look idle for some browsers. What is the most likely cause?
options: The tests have too many assertions
Requested capabilities (browser name, version or platform) do not match any free node slot, so requests wait for a node that matches
Grid only runs one test at a time
The hub must be restarted every hour
questions.explanation: The Grid distributor matches capabilities to node slots. A request for, say, a specific browserVersion or platformName that no idle node offers stays in the queue.

questions.prompt: You need to capture browser console errors during Selenium tests in Chrome and Firefox. What is the forward-looking approach?
options: Use WebDriver BiDi log events (via Selenium's BiDi/log inspection APIs), which are cross-browser, instead of Chrome-only CDP calls
Read the HTML source for errors
questions.explanation: BiDi standardises event subscriptions such as console logs across browsers. CDP is Chromium-specific and not the long-term cross-browser path.

coding.title: Build a new-session payload
coding.prompt:
Write `new_session(browser, headless=False, extra=None)` that returns the JSON body (as a dict) the client sends to `POST /session`:

```python
{'capabilities': {'alwaysMatch': {'browserName': 'chrome', ...}}}
```

- `browserName` is the browser in lower case.
- If headless and browser is chrome, add `'goog:chromeOptions': {'args': ['--headless=new']}`; for firefox add `'moz:firefoxOptions': {'args': ['-headless']}`.
- Merge any `extra` dict of capabilities into alwaysMatch.
- Raise `ValueError` for browsers other than chrome, firefox, edge (edge uses browserName `MicrosoftEdge`).
coding.explanation: W3C sessions are negotiated with a capabilities object; alwaysMatch holds requirements for every match. Vendor-specific options use prefixed keys such as goog:chromeOptions, which is how the protocol stays standard while allowing browser-specific settings.
hints: Normalise with browser.lower() and map to the official browserName.
Vendor options go under prefixed keys: goog:chromeOptions, moz:firefoxOptions.

coding.title: Map commands to W3C endpoints
coding.prompt:
Write `toRequest(sessionId, command, args)` returning `{ method, path, body }` for these W3C WebDriver commands:

| command | method | path | body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get` | POST | `/session/{id}/url` | `{ url: args.url }` |
| `findElement` | POST | `/session/{id}/element` | `{ using, value }` |
| `click` | POST | `/session/{id}/element/{elementId}/click` | `{}` |
| `getTitle` | GET | `/session/{id}/title` | `null` |
| `quit` | DELETE | `/session/{id}` | `null` |

For `findElement`, `args` is `{ by, value }` with `by` one of `id`, `css`, `xpath`; translate `id` to `{ using: 'css selector', value: '#' + value }`, `css` to `css selector`, and `xpath` to `xpath`. Unknown commands throw an Error.
coding.explanation: This is the client-side half of Selenium's architecture: every API call becomes an HTTP request against the session. Translating By.id into a CSS selector mirrors what the real clients do, because W3C WebDriver has no 'id' location strategy. Deleting the session is how quit() ends it.
hints: A switch on the command name keeps the mapping readable.
For findElement, map 'id' to ['css selector', '#' + value].

tests.name: click, quit and unknown
tests.code: assertEqual(toRequest('s','click',{elementId:'e1'}).path, '/session/s/element/e1/click'); assertEqual(toRequest('s','quit').method, 'DELETE'); let m=''; try { toRequest('s','hover'); } catch(e) { m = e.message; } assert(m.includes('unknown'), 'unknown command should throw')
